newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Bell proposes upping svc prices.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Bell proposes upping svc prices.

text.p: Cincinnati Bell Inc's Cincinnati Bell Telephone said on Monday it would propose increasing residence-service prices closer to actual cost, as part of a plan to make it a more competitive provider.
The company also said it would propose adopting cost-based prices for interconnecting its telecommunications networks with networks of other telecommunications companies.
The plan was outlined in a notice Cincinnati Bell said it filed on Monday with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.
The company said it intended to deliver its complete proposal -- so called "Commitment 2000" -- to the commission on January 29.
Under the plan, Cincinnati Telephone said it would propose gradually eliminating subsidies from business-service prices and raising residence-service prices closer to real cost.
Increases in residence-customer prices would be phased in over two years, with limits on the amount of increase in any one year, it said.
As for adopting cost-based interconnection prices, the company said it also proposed selling elements of its networks to competitors on a wholesale basis.
The terms and prices assume commission approval of Cincinnati Telephone's request for exemption from some federal and state regulatory guidelines, it said.
The company also said it would propose creating categories for services to determine future pricing.

Finally, it said it would propose establishing a provision for an access revenue surcharge to be assessed on each access line in Ohio until the subsidy paid by interexchange carriers is addressed by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission and the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.
The company said it was essential to increase residence-customer prices in light of recent regulatory changes.
